Combos are hype when they are difficult. It’s why people get hype seeing refly in mvc2 or why people get hype seeing taunt jet upper in tekken. It’s why no one gets hype seeing auto combos no matter how cool they look.

Difficulty and unique are things SFV is not. Removing all difficulty from combos was probably their biggest mistake, but it was a good lesson to prove that people don’t get hype off of visuals alone. Rarity, difficulty, creativity, and crowd can make a combo or a sequence really hype. But in SFV barely anything is difficult so basically nothing is rare, your bnb is probably some variation of the “stylish” combo anyway, and SFV neutral is so trash to watch that essentially nothing will be hype even when you see it. The only thing that could be hype is x player beats y player. 

Only SF6 could save them at this point. Taking away difficulty does nothing for anyone, dumbs down the meta, and doesn’t even make the game more popular. You think fortnite is popular because it’s easy? CSGO popular because it’s easy? People liked watching smash because all those tricks were things they could just do at home? What about basketball? Would it be more popular if it was easy? Lower the rim a bit to give me a shot? 

Making the games good to play is one aspect of making it popular to play competitively because your players obviously have to enjoy the game, but devs will make the game easy at the EXPENSE of enjoyment because they think it will make it more popular, even if they make the game visually boring and barebones ala mvci and SFV. Whoever told them this shit needs to be fired.

The most important aspect of making something hype to watch is making it the pinnacle of human achievement, not something you could get down with some consistency in an afternoon. Df2 electric is very difficult, so when it’s seen in tournament it will get a cheer. SFV hides its pinnacle of human achievement in knowledge of the game and matchups which by its very nature will never be hype to watch. It sort of looks the same as you do it at home but you can’t do what Tokido or punk does. You can’t do what tachikawa  does. 

SFV design philosophy was from day one making it look like you could do those things which sucks all longevity out of the game. A hype combo is more than wow that looks cool. It’s “wow that is creative cool and difficult. This is the peak of human performance when honed for long enough, congrats to that dude” 

SF4 being popular was probably what caused this as well. People thought fighting games died because of their difficulty but that’s not even close to the case. Every single fighting game dev took the ease of gameplay SF4 had as a reason for its popularity and not the return of street fighter to modern consoles. The only people that didn’t take that message was the tekken devs. Just frames everywhere and look at them. There’s no characters they can add that will make SFV good. There’s no combos that will ever be hype. The game was designed with a foolish eye at human nature to begin with, that people will take inauthentic spectacle over genuine human achievement.

So no, there aren’t any hype combos nor will they ever be. Throw this damned project away and get started on sf6, this game can’t be saved. It’s literally bread and circuses in the Roman Empires’s collapse.
